detail.abstract:
The five largest U.S. technology firms spent $380 billion on capital expenditure in 2025 and are forecast to spend roughly double that in 2026. These firms risk bankruptcy unless expected profits grow commensurately. We embed this observation in a two-sector open-economy model with rare productivity booms. We calibrate the boom size to match the observed increase in investment projected through 2027, implying that a boom raises AI-sector productivity by a factor of roughly 2.7. We then calibrate a two-year window of a 50% annual probability of an increase of the same magnitude, generating a range of scenarios consistent with the wide variety of industry forecasts, along with an elevated permanent probability tied to the valuation of the aggregate market. The implied additional cumulative GDP growth ranges from 5 to 58 percentage points by 2030, with AI shares of the economy ranging from 8% to 39%. Long-term annual growth is in expectation approximately 7% but with substantial risk. With risk aversion of 3, and an elasticity of intertemporal substitution equal to 1, the risk-free rate increases by approximately half a percentage point, and the equity premium rises by approximately 3 percentage points.

title: Fixed Payoffs and Floating Prices: Self-Fulfilling Bubbles in On-Chain Prediction Markets

detail.title: Fixed Payoffs and Floating Prices: Self-Fulfilling Bubbles in On-Chain Prediction Markets
detail.abstract: We show that overpricing in on-chain prediction markets is self-fulfilling: for the same fundamentals, a bubble and a no-bubble equilibrium coexist. The bubble survives only for longshots, and a global-games refinement selects a unique tipping point. The cause is institutional. A one-dollar cap and a two-sided market seem to let a contrarian short an overpriced contract via the complementary token, but that short is fully collateralized with no credit, so disciplining a longshot ties up nearly a dollar and invites a squeeze, making discipline a coordination problem. Capital-weighted clearing underprices favorites. We prove uniqueness and identify levers that restore discipline.

detail.title: Reducing Gun Violence at Scale

publicationDetails.journalName: NBER Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Baltimore's homicide rate fell by roughly 60% between 2022 and 2025, an exceptional decline among large U.S. cities. At the start of this period, Baltimore launched a strategy that concentrated police and social service resources on a small set of people thought to be driving group-involved gun violence. The approach—“focused deterrence”—has been implemented in some form by cities across the U.S. The strategy was introduced first in the Western police district, one of the highest-violence communities in the U.S. Relative to comparable Baltimore neighborhoods, we estimate that within 18 months shootings and homicides in the Western district fell by roughly one third and carjackings by about 40%, with no spillovers elsewhere in the city. These gains came without expanding overall enforcement: total arrests were flat even as arrests for serious violent crimes rose sharply, indicating that the strategy redirected police authority toward serious violence rather than widening the net of the justice system. Person-level and qualitative evidence point to deterrence, incapacitation, services, and community messengers' legitimacy as contributing channels, with no single mechanism explaining the bulk of the decline. The social value of the averted violence is roughly 35 times the program's first-year spending. Citywide, Baltimore's homicide rate over this period was about 25% below a synthetic counterfactual built from other large cities. The timing of Baltimore's homicide decline and the absence of a larger-than-expected drop in other violent crimes are consistent with the expansion of focused deterrence across the city and a broader shift toward a targeted, partnership-based response to group violence. Baltimore's experience offers an important blueprint for how cities can achieve reductions in gun violence at scale.

detail.title: From Financial Crisis to Pandemic Shock: A Pixel-Level Assessment of Multidimensional Socioeconomic Impact and Resilience in the Nile River Basin
detail.abstract: Global crises pose severe challenges to the sustainable development of ecologically fragile regions. However, constrained by the coarse granularity and scarcity of traditional statistical data, it is difficult to precisely characterize the spatiotemporal evolution of multidimensional socioeconomic impacts in these regions under crises. To address these data limitations, this study constructs a transferable pixel-level multidimensional assessment framework, conducting an in-depth comparative analysis of the socioeconomic impacts of two major events in the Nile River Basin: the 2008 Global Financial Crisis (GFC) and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic. Based on the Growth-Poverty-Inequality (GPI) trilemma theory, the study integrates nighttime light remote sensing data with multisource socioeconomic spatial indicators to construct the Economic Impact Index (EII), quantifying regional economic dynamics and class mobility. It further derives the Economic Shock Resilience Index (ESR) to comprehensively assess the relative shock-absorbing capacity of various regions within the basin. The study finds: (1) Regarding impact characteristics, the GFC triggered larger fluctuations with significant spatial differentiation (impact intensity was approximately 4.1 times that of the COVID-19 pandemic), but it propelled only a very small proportion (1.91%) of the population into higher-income groups. In contrast, the economic contraction during the initial phase of the COVID-19 pandemic exhibited strong synchronicity across the entire region, with income class mobility nearly stagnating. (2) Regarding resilience evolution, the basin exhibits significant divergent pathways: regions with stronger infrastructure support and higher levels of digitalization achieved continuous leaps in resilience, while regions affected by geopolitical conflicts fell into a state of long-term, high-vulnerability lock-in. The spatial assessment framework proposed in this study not only provides a method for spatially quantifying crisis impacts in data-scarce regions but also a GeoAI-compatible and spatially explicit analytical foundation for targeted post-crisis recovery prioritization and resilience-oriented policy design.

affiliations: and New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: Prediction Markets as Shadow Financial Markets: Completion, Risk Migration, and the Limits of Product-Based Regulation
detail.abstract: An event contract paying one dollar on a verifiable event is an Arrow security. We ask when listing completes the financial system and when it shadows it, relocating already-spanned risk. Everything turns on exposure-blindness: a fungible binary cannot condition on its holder. A contract's class depends on the configuration, not the instrument; no product-based rule classifies it. Because pooling makes liquidity coordinative, identical fundamentals support a shadow and a latent regime, and tightening the regulated venue tips the economy into the former. Because a salient event's price moves its own probability, insuring it manufactures the loss. Regulation must be function-based.

title: Rehypothecated Security: How Restaking Manufactures the Fragility It Promises to Prevent

detail.title: Rehypothecated Security: How Restaking Manufactures the Fragility It Promises to Prevent
detail.abstract: Restaking lets one bonded stake secure many services, promising capital efficiency. We model it as rehypothecation of a finite pool of slashable collateral, a form of fractional-reserve banking. Per-service collateralization does not ensure safety: the binding constraint is the tail of simultaneous corruption, so the safe reuse ratio is the inverse of corruption-risk diversification. This correlation is not exogenous. Reuse manufactures it, because over-reuse makes coordinated attacks profitable and leads attackers to create common-mode vulnerabilities. Safety is thus self-fulfilling below a leverage frontier and self-defeating above it. The corrective is a capital requirement keyed to induced, not prevailing, correlation.

title: Solvent Runs on Fully Collateralized On-Chain Platforms: A Global-Games Theory of Prediction-Market Redemption
affiliations: and New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: Solvent Runs on Fully Collateralized On-Chain Platforms: A Global-Games Theory of Prediction-Market Redemption
detail.abstract: Tokenized redeemable claims (stablecoins, custodial exchanges, on-chain prediction markets) are thought run-proof because fully collateralized. This confuses a contract-level with a platform-level property: full backing says nothing about the pool's liquid, recoverable value. In a global game we prove a unique threshold equilibrium in which fully collateralized, even over-collateralized, platforms run. Because redemption settles before resolution, better information aggregation worsens runs, reversing the banking logic; we prove an aggregation-stability frontier with a closed-form ceiling beyond which a par-redeemable market runs, removed only by mark-to-market redemption, which surrenders money-likeness. USDC's 2023 de-peg (a solvent platform that nonetheless ran) calibrates the mechanism.

title: Does Tokenization Democratize IPO Access? Adverse Selection and Allocative Efficiency in Tokenized Securities Markets

detail.title: Does Tokenization Democratize IPO Access? Adverse Selection and Allocative Efficiency in Tokenized Securities Markets
detail.abstract: Tokenized issuance gives securities a cheap, open venue as an alternative to costly certified intermediation. Privately informed issuers choose between them: certification reveals quality, while the open venue pools. High types certify and low types tokenize, so the open venue signals low quality. Cheaper tokenization does not flood the pool with lemons; it raises pool quality, but it draws the best issuers out of certification, so the market produces less information. Whether welfare falls turns on why certification matters: firms certify to be priced accurately, which mainly redistributes value, while society values certification because it allocates capital. When the private motive dominates, the market over-certifies and cheaper tokenization is a correction; otherwise it is harmful. Optimal policy can be a subsidy as readily as a tax.

title: Machine Learning for Predicting Hospital Length of Stay and Resource Utilization: A Systematic Review of EHR-Based Models

detail.title: Machine Learning for Predicting Hospital Length of Stay and Resource Utilization: A Systematic Review of EHR-Based Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract:
Objectives
To systematically evaluate performance, methodological quality and clinical readiness of machine learning models using electronic health record data for prediction of hospital length of stay and resource use. 

Methods
A comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore was performed for studies published from January 2010 to April 2025, following PRISMA guidelines and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO: CRD42024595877). Eligibility was defined by the PICOTS framework with emphasis on adult and pediatric acute care patients. Data extraction was performed according to the CHARMS checklist and the methodological quality was assessed by the PROBAST tool.

Results 
Of the 1,304 records found, 86 studies satisfied the requirements for inclusion. The best discriminative performance was achieved with non-linear ensemble models based on trees (XGBoost, Gradient Boosting Machines and Random Forests) with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values between 0.75 and 0.89 for the binary classification of prolonged stays. Models that included natural language processing of clinical narratives across multiple modalities increased accuracy further by capturing psychosocial barriers to discharge. However, more than 90% of the included studies were at high risk of bias, driven by poor handling of missing data, lack of external validation, and poor reporting of calibration.

Discussion 
Current models are highly discriminative but suffer from pervasive methodological weaknesses that severely limit their clinical readiness. Future work should involve rigorous multi-center external validation, the integration of machine learning operations pipelines for continuous model monitoring and recalibration, and fairness-aware algorithmic design to ensure equitable deployment across diverse healthcare settings.

title: Prudential Liquidity Rules beyond Banking: Evidence from Refundable Deposit Funding for Residential Care Providers
affiliations: UNSW Business School, UNSW Business School, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Prudential Liquidity Rules beyond Banking: Evidence from Refundable Deposit Funding for Residential Care Providers
detail.abstract: While the structural mismatch between illiquid assets and demandable liabilities is a source of fragility in traditional banking, this capital--liquidity tradeoff is migrating to the non-banking sector, emerging as a vulnerability in the global aged care industry. Unlike traditional banks, aged care providers are highly exposed to demographic and mortality shocks. A crisis such as the COVID-19 pandemic can reduce occupancy, depressing operating cash flows and triggering large-scale refunds of deposit-like accommodation balances. Using Australia’s newly introduced Minimum Liquidity Amount (MLA) regulation as a prime empirical setting, this paper evaluates rigid, one-size-fits-all liquidity buffers against forward-looking, stress-based frameworks. We develop a stochastic simulation model that integrates resident flows with macroeconomic conditions and provider balance-sheet dynamics, utilising a continuous-time Markov chain. The analysis of representative providers reveals that the uniform application of the default MLA misaligns with true liquidity risk profiles: it imposes excessive regulatory constraints on larger providers while remaining insufficiently stringent for smaller ones. To address these limitations, a risk-sensitive MLA framework is proposed, calibrated via a multidimensional stress testing procedure which replicates the regime shifts induced by exogenous shocks. Expressed as a linear, balance-sheet-based rule, the risk-sensitive framework preserves crisis resilience while expanding the capital--liquidity frontier across the aged care sector. By integrating stress-test-based foundations within a transparent rule, it offers a transferable template for prudential regulation beyond the banking perimeter.

title: Corporate Culture, Misconduct, and the Hypocrisy Penalty
affiliations: and New York University (NYU) - Leonard N. Stern School of Business

detail.title: Corporate Culture, Misconduct, and the Hypocrisy Penalty
detail.abstract: We model corporate culture as two choices: substantive investment in internal controls that prevent misconduct, and public claims that shape stakeholder beliefs. Because substance is revealed only at detection, firms can claim more than they deliver. Stakeholders penalize the exposed gap as hypocrisy, so the firms that claim most face the largest sanctions, reversing standard signaling predictions. This penalty is self-disciplining: weakening it lowers substantive investment and raises misconduct. Industry credibility is a depletable commons prone to collapse. Detection endogeneity biases misconduct regressions, and first-best requires two instruments (a subsidy on substantive investment in internal controls and a tax on symbolic claims).

title: Runs on Artificial Intelligence Platforms

detail.title: Runs on Artificial Intelligence Platforms

keywords: platform-run risk premium JEL classification: G01

detail.abstract: An AI platform produces its quality from participation withdrawable on demand. Because its most informative contributors are its most mobile, a confidence shock strips the best data first, so quality falls faster than headcount. A global-games refinement gives a unique equilibrium with an exact average-quality threshold, an endogenous run probability, and a panic component priced when runs fall in high-marginal-utility states. Three results depart from the networkeffects-as-moats benchmark: fragility is set by the sensitivity of quality to participation, not its level; it is hump-shaped in network intensity; and platform equity carries a left-tail disaster component scaled by the panic width.

title: Methodological Challenges in Nutritional Epidemiology: A Causal Inference Perspective
affiliations: , Qatar University - Human Nutrition Department and Adelaide University

detail.title: Methodological Challenges in Nutritional Epidemiology: A Causal Inference Perspective

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest. The funders had no role in the design of the study; in the collection, analyses, or interpretation of data; in the writing of the manuscript; or in the decision to publish the results.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia (NHMRC) Investigator Grants to YAM (#2009776) and EH (#2025349).

detail.abstract: Nutritional epidemiology is central to dietary guidance, yet causal interpretation remains challenging because diet is multidimensional, compositional, time-varying, socially patterned, and difficult to measure. This perspective examines key methodological challenges through a causal inference lens, with emphasis on the distinction between association and causation, the definition of causal estimands, and the assumptions required for identification and estimation. We discuss challenges across the research process, including the limitations of long-term randomised trials, dietary measurement error, geographical and temporal variation in diet, co-consumption and substitution among dietary components, ambiguity in defining dietary strategies, confounding and effect modification, selection mechanisms, and energy adjustment. We also consider how interpretation, evidence synthesis, dissemination, and policy translation can be distorted when studies with different estimands, populations, exposure definitions, comparators, or time horizons are treated as equivalent. Observational studies remain essential for evaluating long-term diet-disease relationships that cannot be fully addressed by trials, but their value depends on sharper causal questions, explicit estimand definition, appropriate methods, and cautious interpretation. Apparent inconsistencies in nutritional epidemiology may therefore reflect not only biological uncertainty, but also differences in exposure definitions, comparators, time scales, energy adjustment, confounding structures, measurement error, and analytic choices. Strengthening the field requires closer alignment between causal questions, methods, biological plausibility, and real-world dietary decisions.

title: Discovering the Historical Anglo-American Constitution
affiliations: Georgia State University - College of Law

detail.title: Discovering the Historical Anglo-American Constitution
detail.abstract: The controversy over birthright citizenship in the United States and the meaning of the Fourteenth Amendment has exposed two urgent needs in American constitutional scholarship: a meticulous account of the history of the law of natural-born subjects and citizens, and a rigorous methodology for responsibly engaging with constitutional developments over long periods. This article answers both. It advances the "historical constitution" as a framework for assessing longarc legal developments, attending at once to continuity and change, to the form and formation of law, and to legal and socio-political authority-the high law and the low law. The framework gives American constitutional scholars a disciplined approach to Anglo-American inquiry, one that asks how law operated across time rather than at isolated moments. Drawing on rich archival sources, Year Book entries, and Privy Council records-including the original manuscript record of Calvin's Case-it demonstrates that the territorial rule of birthright citizenship held with remarkable consistency across five English legal systems, surviving political, social, and economic pressures alike. The article traces that principle's transatlantic journey to the Americas, illuminating what the historical constitution reveals about national identity and citizenship at the origins of constitutionalism in the United States. The method's promise extends well beyond this Article; its utility is not exhausted by the question that occasions it.

title: Scenario Based Government Training: Operationalizing Epistemic Accountability through Auditable Institutional Reasoning: The ELENA Framework

detail.title: Scenario Based Government Training: Operationalizing Epistemic Accountability through Auditable Institutional Reasoning: The ELENA Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Independent Research
declarations.funderStatement: Independent Research

detail.abstract: Governments face pressure to modernize how they train their workforce without giving up on accountability, procedural consistency, or public trust. Existing international frameworks for AI in government employee training (Balbo di Vinadio et al., 2022; OECD, 2025) and parallel work on public educational cognitive infrastructure (Li, Zhao, Wang, & Hu, 2026) operate at the level of principle, addressing educational AI broadly rather than the specific demands of public sector training where outputs shape how government employees interpret rules with statutory, regulatory, and citizen facing consequences. This paper offers a conceptual framework, ELENA (Epistemic Learning Environment with Notated Accountability, in Spanish Entorno de Lecciones Epistémicas con Notación Auditable), organized around four core principles, namely adaptive learning, hierarchical knowledge organization, source based accountability, and linguistic parity, and works them into a single architecture for government employee training, then exemplifies it for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. AI is treated as a bounded instructional facilitator that supports a learner's engagement with structured, source anchored knowledge but does not displace institutional review. This paper focuses on three practical aspects. First, it turns four broad design principles into a framework that can actually be tested. In particular, it introduces the Concept Domain Claim (CDC) trace, a structured record that links each system output to its sources, version history, confidence level, and instructional context. Where the Open Cognitive Graph proposed by Li et al. (2026) maps pedagogical structure, the CDC trace serves a different and complementary purpose, an accountability tool for institutional training environments organized around legal authority rather than instructional sequence. Second, the paper shows how ELENA relates to existing frameworks by comparing it across key dimensions such as knowledge architecture, accountability mechanisms, and evaluation. Third, it grounds the framework in Puerto Rico's public sector context, including the island's seventy eight municipalities, centralized executive-branch human resources structure, bilingual working environment, and proposed evaluation pathway. Read together, these features support the broader argument that government training systems of this kind should be treated as part of public cognitive infrastructure, with the same expectation of accountability and review that applies to other public institutions.

title: The Enforcement Overload Hypothesis: Dynamic Balance and Cooperation Suppression in Collaborative Systems

detail.title: The Enforcement Overload Hypothesis: Dynamic Balance and Cooperation Suppression in Collaborative Systems
detail.abstract:
Human cooperation depends on trust, reciprocity, contribution visibility, and mechanisms for detecting and sanctioning free-riding. However, the same enforcement mechanisms that protect cooperation may also suppress it when they become excessive, poorly calibrated, or socially threatening.

This paper proposes the Enforcement Overload Hypothesis: cooperative participation declines when the perceived cognitive, affective, reputational, and institutional costs of maintaining fair participation exceed the expected benefits of contributing. The paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding this second-order fragility of collaborative systems. 
It argues that visible or expected free-riding can increase perceived monitoring burden, which in turn raises cognitive load, social evaluative threat, reputational defensiveness, and participation costs. Under such conditions, honest contributors may withdraw, reduce effort, avoid risk, or shift into defensive forms of participation. 

The framework identifies two reinforcing mechanisms: The Prosocial Suppression Loop, in which insufficient positive reinforcement for honest contribution leads to reduced participation and stronger control, and the Controller Problem, in which some participants may derive status, moral validation, or psychological reward from monitoring and sanctioning rather than contributing.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Energy Financial Risk Meter (EFRM), a sector-specific systemic risk indicator for the European Union's energy sector. The EFRM is constructed by applying LASSO quantile regression to daily stock returns and market capitalisation data from 100 major European energy companies, while also integrating a set of economic variables and a geopolitical risk index as exogenous drivers. The EFRM index captures major systemic events in the energy markets, namely the 2020 COVID pandemic and the 2022 Russia-Ukraine war. By employing rolling-window VAR and time-varying parameter VAR (TVP-VAR) estimations across monthly and daily frequencies, we document the activation of a previously dormant geopolitical-to-energy-risk transmission channel and the subsequent material attenuation of downstream transmission to European equity and credit markets. Cross-continental validation using US Treasury yields and the US Energy SPDR ETF confirms the global external validity of the EFRM signal. From a practical perspective, the proposed indicator offers policymakers, regulators, and financial stability authorities a high-frequency tool for early detection of systemic threats in one of the most critical components of the EU economy.

title: Paradox of Privilege for Asian Guestworkers in Silicon Valley, 51 B.Y.U. Law Review
affiliations: UC Law, San Francisco

detail.title: Paradox of Privilege for Asian Guestworkers in Silicon Valley, 51 B.Y.U. Law Review
detail.abstract: This Article examines the liminality of temporary workers in the technology industry. Based on the experiences of technology workers who hold the H-1B work visa at prominent tech companies in Silicon Valley, it identifies a "paradox of privilege," wherein the construction of temporary work visas ensures skilled workers simultaneously enjoy privileged status-through lawful status, education, and technical skills-and suffer from profound vulnerability to legal, economic, and racial subordination due to their dual dependence on private employers and a burdensome bureaucracy to maintain their legality and livelihood. Drawing on original interviews with thirtytwo technology workers, I demonstrate how intersecting legal liminality, economic precarity, and racial hierarchy position predominantly Asian tech workers similarly to their domestic counterparts: Asians and Asian American laborers, who are the descendants and diaspora of "coolie laborers" during the Chinese exclusion era. Their intertwined subordination leads to a social construction of their temporary visa that renders Asian tech workers impermanent, even though the legal design of the visa is colorblind and enables a formal path to citizenship. The paradox of their formal and social position status is resolved by the post-hoc rationalization of immigration law as the mechanism for the exclusion of Asian tech workers, which in turn animates the inequitable design of the temporary visa.

detail.abstract: The outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza in Great Britain over the last five years represent the most prolonged and severe period of virus activity recorded in the country, prompting renewed scrutiny of how biosecurity is conceptualised and practised within poultry systems. This paper examines how the structure of poultry sectors, producing meat, eggs, and game birds, shape disease risk and the possibilities for a resilient poultry ecology. Using a production and distribution network approach, we combine a desk-based review of industry, policy, grey, and published literature with qualitative data from 19 in-depth interviews, supplemented by field visits and engagement in stakeholder events. Our analysis shows that highly integrated and geographically concentrated poultry meat and layer systems interact with wild and semi-wild birds in ways which generate distinct challenges. Concentration of production and processing infrastructure, aging housing stock, consumer demand for freerange, and large-scale releases of game birds impact decisions around poultry governance and questions of risk around avian influenza incursion. We identify two cross-cutting 'entanglements' that condition avian influenza virus vulnerability: (1) poultry planning, where fragmented and often contested land-use decisions interact with environmental and biodiversity policies to shape exposure to wild and semi-wild ecologies; and (2) the insuring of poultry ecologies, where a market failure in private avian influenza insurance and uneven and contested state compensation regimes differentially distribute risk across producers and sectors. We argue that farm-level biosecurity, while necessary, is insufficient to secure Britain's poultry production under near-endemic avian influenza virus pressure. A more bio-resilient poultry future will require macro-level, multi-sectoral coordination that integrates spatial planning, infrastructure renewal, and equitable risk-sharing mechanisms for disease preparedness.

title: The Breakdown of a Ceasefire: Evidence on Dynamic Beliefs About Peace in the Israel-Hamas War
affiliations: Charles University in Prague - Faculty of Law

detail.title: The Breakdown of a Ceasefire: Evidence on Dynamic Beliefs About Peace in the Israel-Hamas War
detail.abstract: This paper examines dynamic beliefs about peace in the wake of violent conflict during the Israel-Hamas war. I leverage the staggered timing in the roll-out of the Israel National Election Studies survey, relative to the breakdown of a two-month-long ceasefire in March 2025, in a difference-in-differences specification for estimation. I find a short-lived effect, ranging from a 4.19 to 8.38 percentage point decline, in respondents' beliefs that peace is possible. I attribute the baseline result to group-level social identity, with respondents who do not directly know someone harmed by Hamas driving the effect. I rule out other forms of social cohesion, including eroding trust in leadership and cooperation via political protest, as well as alternative explanations such as changes in media consumption and/or issue prioritization around the breakdown of the ceasefire.

title: GCM-MAE: Breaking the Reconstruction Trap in Endoscopy via De-pixelized Contextual Mimicry
affiliations: Ocean University of China, Army Medical University, Government of the People's Republic of China - Army Medical University, Government of the People's Republic of China - Army Medical University, Ocean University of China, Army Medical University, Griffith University and Government of the People's Republic of China - Department of Gastroenterology

detail.title: GCM-MAE: Breaking the Reconstruction Trap in Endoscopy via De-pixelized Contextual Mimicry
detail.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) in gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is often stifled by the Reconstruction Trap: the traditional mandate of pixel-level recovery forces models to prioritize domain-specific visual disturbances over latent pathological semantics. Motivated by the spectral bias of neural networks, we hypothesize and provide empirical evidence that the pixel-reconstruction objective serves as a “gradient anchor”, steering optimization toward local texture memorization instead of robust lesion-level abstraction. To break this dependency, we define a new pre-training paradigm, Guided Contextual Mimicry (GCM). Building on MAE, we introduce GCM-MAE, a fully Depixelized framework that replaces signal reconstruction with manifold-targeted alignment. As a result, the Gradient Anchor induced by reconstruction is removed, allowing the encoder to converge toward a noise-invariant semantic representation manifold. Central to our approach is Saliency-Preservation Sampling (SPS), an attentionguided inverse-sampling strategy that rejects dominant mucosal noise while distilling sparse pathological signals. Extensive experiments show that GCM-MAE consistently outperforms all compared SSL baselines, achieving 88.94% AP50 on Kvasir-SEG and a +12.54 AP gain in cross-dataset generalization on multi-center datasets. These re- sults suggest that in high-noise clinical environments, semantic purification on a de- pixelized manifold is fundamentally superior to signal reconstruction.

title: Public Administration as an Upstream Variable: A Measurement Framework Beyond Service Satisfaction

detail.title: Public Administration as an Upstream Variable: A Measurement Framework Beyond Service Satisfaction

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual paper introducing a measurement framework. No empirical data were collected.

detail.abstract: Public administrations across advanced democracies remain institutionally capable. Anti-institutional populism nonetheless persists and, in some cases, intensifies. Existing explanations emphasise economic dislocation, cultural backlash, and partisan strategy. Public administration has been studied mainly as something populist governments challenge. This paper examines it as a potential upstream variable: a factor shaping the structural conditions under which populist mobilisation becomes more likely. The paper introduces four constructs at the intersection of three scholarly traditions: the PA-populism literature, the citizen satisfaction tradition, and the governance gap literature. Civic-relational capacity is the analytical condition: the extent to which institutions are perceived as present in the domains citizens experience as most consequential. The displacement hypothesis is the historical claim that this capacity has been gradually eroded by cumulative administrative reform. The expectation-recognition gap (ERG) is the primary measurement construct, capturing the divergence between how the same citizen evaluates the same institution through a needs-anchored frame and a service-based frame. Institutional legibility is a secondary measurement construct, derived from the same survey architecture, capturing whether citizens can locate the institutions formally responsible for their concerns. The four are nested rather than competing: one analytical condition, one historical claim about it, and two measurement constructs derived from a single survey architecture that make it observable. This is an agenda-setting paper. It introduces constructs and a measurement logic; it does not test them. No cross-national claim should be read as empirically verified. The contribution lies in making a previously unmeasured dimension of democratic life observable: whether institutional activity aligns with what citizens themselves identify as most pressing. Beyond the research programme, the same architecture functions as a practical diagnostic. Any public administration can adapt it to assess where its activities align with citizens' expressed concerns and where they do not.

title: Macro-Release Inventory and Event-Gated Forecast Correction in VIX-Implied Variance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Macro-Release Inventory and Event-Gated Forecast Correction in VIX-Implied Variance
detail.abstract: Prior research shows that scheduled macroeconomic announcements affect implied volatility, but less is known about whether release calendars create systematic forecast-error states for standard VIX-implied variance models. This paper studies that question by constructing a macro-release inventory mismatch measure for CPI and nonfarm payroll announcements. The measure separates stale release inventory embedded in historical HAR-IV inputs from future release pressure associated with upcoming scheduled releases, and converts their difference into a normalized release-mismatch indicator, NRMI. The correction is implemented through an event-gated forecasting rule: forecasts are modified only when the next trading day contains a CPI or NFP release, while nonevent-day forecasts remain equal to the recursive HAR-IV benchmark. Using daily VIX data from 1990 to 2024 and 866 scheduled releases, the gated NRMI model improves one-day future CPI/NFP-window forecasts by 1.416% in MSE, 3.543% in MAE, and 0.034% in QLIKE, with Diebold-Mariano p-values of 0.014 and 0.012 for MSE and QLIKE. The evidence supports a targeted event-window correction interpretation: macro-release inventory helps explain and correct oneday HAR-IV forecast errors around scheduled releases, but it is not a universal multi-horizon VIX forecasting factor and does not uniformly dominate eventdummy corrections.

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Productivity Change — Evidence from a DEA-Malmquist Analysis

detail.abstract: This study examines whether firm-level artificial intelligence (AI) integration leads to sustained improvements in firm productivity. Using the DEA-Malmquist model, we estimate firm productivity change and its two components, technical progress and relative efficiency change. We measure AI integration using a textual measure of AI-related keywords disclosed in annual reports. Results show that AI integration is positively associated with productivity growth, driven by both technical progress (innovation effect) and improvements in relative efficiency (catching-up effect). These effects persist over subsequent periods. Further analyses show that human capital mediates the effect of AI integration on productivity change, while technological innovation mediates its effect on productivity change and technical progress. Additionally, state-owned enterprises (SOEs), non-high-tech firms, and firms in low-marketization regions gain productivity growth through technical progress, while non-SOEs, high-tech firms and firms in regions with higher marketization levels mainly benefit from improvements in relative efficiency. We also find that AI integration improves productivity through both components in regions with stronger intellectual property protection, but mainly through technical progress in regions with weaker protection. Overall, our study highlights that firm-level AI integration drives dynamic productivity growth, which is realized through both frontier-shifting innovation and catching-up to best practices.

title: Dynamic Multi-Pair Trading Strategy in Cryptocurrency Markets with Deep Reinforcement Learning

detail.title: Dynamic Multi-Pair Trading Strategy in Cryptocurrency Markets with Deep Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: This study aims to determine whether the application of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) as a specialized execution overlay can enhance pair trading in highly volatile cryptocurrency markets. Although classical implementations of the strategy have proven successful in traditional equities, they frequently exhibit rigidity and suffer from severe divergence risks when applied to high-variance environments. To address this need, this research introduces novel concepts. To construct a robust system, we developed a hierarchical "Filter-then-Rank" pair selection methodology and a proprietary "Fixed Risk, Adaptive Mean" execution model. The system employs a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layer to govern execution decisions within strict deterministic risk management boundaries. Evaluated on 1-hour interval data from the Binance USD-M Futures market, the optimized RL policy achieved an Out-Of-Sample performance that substantially outperformed the heuristic baseline. A stationary circular block bootstrap robustness check confirms that the Agent's risk-adjusted outperformance is statistically significant at the 10% level. Although falling marginally short of the stricter 5% threshold, this result highlights the extreme idiosyncratic variance characteristic of digital assets. Ultimately, this thesis contributes to the quantitative finance literature by introducing a hybrid architecture that combines statistical arbitrage with DRL execution policies. Furthermore, it delivers a novel framework for safe reinforcement learning via deterministic shielding, proving that anchoring a neural policy to statistically robust boundaries successfully mitigates severe divergence risks.

detail.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence-autonomous systems that plan across multiple steps and act in dynamic environments without human direction-has begun to be integrated in a material way into the operations of companies around the world. Its deployment highlights the limits of the classical principal-agent framework on which modern corporate law rests: agentic AI systems are not utility maximisers, their internal reasoning is not readily seen nor reliably verifiable, and they fall outside the legal and economic categories through which agency doctrine allocates responsibility. This paper argues that directors' fiduciary obligations in respect of agentic AI are best understood through what the paper terms the fiduciary infrastructure: a four-layer account (data, model, deployment, accountability) of the duty of care that directors now owe to their companies in the adoption of agentic AI in their operations. The term is developed through a comparative study of three jurisdictions whose AI governance frameworks together occupy the spectrum of regulatory responses available to advanced economies-the prescriptive EU AI Act, the hybrid Korean AI Basic Act, and Singapore's voluntary Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI-and is anchored in existing corporate-law authorities: Vita Health and Goh Jin Hian in Singapore, Siemens/Neubürger in Germany as representative Member State, and the Daewoo line in South Korea. The paper extends the analysis to investor protection, identifying three distinct enforcement architectures and the novel information asymmetries that agentic AI generates for capital markets, and proposes targeted reforms in corporate law and securities disclosure.

title: K-Waves of Global GDP Per Capita (1961–2024) and GCR Intensity Extremes (1959–2022): R2 = 0.86
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: K-Waves of Global GDP Per Capita (1961–2024) and GCR Intensity Extremes (1959–2022): R2 = 0.86
detail.abstract:
The classical theory of innovation clusters (J. Schumpeter) and the concept of new technological paradigms (S. Yu. Glazyev), which dominate modern macroeconomics, view the emergence of fundamental innovations as the root cause of long waves (K-waves). However, these models leave a key question unanswered: what determines the cyclical nature of innovations and technological paradigms?

This paper proposes an interdisciplinary approach to the nature of long waves. A mathematical model of macrocycles is constructed based on a comparison of data from the Moscow Neutron Monitor on the intensity of galactic cosmic rays (GCR) for 1959–2022 and econometric statistics from the World Bank on global GDP per capita growth for 1961–2024.

The author has identified a very strong correlation between the peak GCR intensity and large business waves (K-waves), where the coupling of processes intensifies to a functional level (R = 0.92).

Unlike J. Schumpeter, who associated cycles with the discrete, wave-like introduction of innovations, and N. Kondratiev, who explained them by the renewal of fixed capital, the author demonstrates that the cyclical nature of innovation is a consequence of periodic changes in the productivity of the human brain. Minimum GCR intensity is accompanied by maximum solar activity and, with an average lag of two years, maximum geomagnetic activity, which desynchronize alpha waves in the brain and reduce the collective cognitive potential of the human population.

Forecast: The author has developed a method for forecasting K-waves of annual growth in global GDP per capita based on the forecast of the Wolf number and GCR intensity, according to which this growth in 2032 will be 2.6%.

title: Effects of Armed Conflict on the Mineral Market: Evidence from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
affiliations: University of Mississippi

detail.title: Effects of Armed Conflict on the Mineral Market: Evidence from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
detail.abstract: This study examines the effect of armed conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) on the price and production of five key minerals. Doing so provides insights into the importance of conflict in the Congo to the global minerals market and, by extension, the global economy. Using data on historical prices and production of cobalt, gold, copper, tin, and silver and the status of armed conflict in the DRC, the author performed multiple regression and interrupted time-series analyses to quantify correlative and causal relationships between the presence of conflict and price, Congolese production, and global production of each mineral. Although the results show that prices and production both generally increase when the DRC is at war, conflict is not a significant cause of these changes. This suggests that conflict in the Congo is not as disruptive to global mineral markets as may be expected.

title: Macroeconomic Determinants of the Nepal Stock Exchange Index: A VECM Approach
affiliations: and Janapriya Multiple Campus

detail.title: Macroeconomic Determinants of the Nepal Stock Exchange Index: A VECM Approach
detail.abstract: This study examines the long-run and short-run relationship between the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index and three core macroeconomic variables-broad money supply (M2), the 91-day Treasury bill rate as a proxy for short-term interest rates, and nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP)-using annual time-series data for the period 1995 to 2022. Augmented Dickey-Fuller tests confirm that all four series are integrated of order one. The Johansen cointegration test identifies one cointegrating equation among the variables, justifying the use of a Vector Error Correction Model (VECM). In the long run, M2 and GDP have positive and statistically significant effects on the NEPSE index, while the interest rate exerts a significant negative effect. Short-run dynamics indicate that money supply positively and the interest rate negatively influence NEPSE within the same year. The error correction term carries a coefficient of-0.94 and is highly significant, indicating that approximately 94 percent of any short-run disequilibrium is corrected within one year. Granger causality runs from money supply and the interest rate to NEPSE, while a feedback effect runs from NEPSE to the interest rate. The model passes serial-correlation, heteroskedasticity, normality and stability diagnostics. The findings support the dividend-discount and quantity-theory channels in the Nepalese context and carry direct implications for monetary policy and financial-stability oversight.

title: Perceived Political Exclusion and Non-Voting Participation Among Rural High School Students in Ontario
affiliations: Trinity College School

detail.title: Perceived Political Exclusion and Non-Voting Participation Among Rural High School Students in Ontario
detail.abstract: This study investigates how perceived political exclusion affects non-voting political participation among rural high school students in Ontario. Drawing on survey data collected from 87 qualifying participants aged 14-17, a Pearson correlation analysis revealed only a weak positive relationship between perceived political inclusion and non-voting participation (r = 0.127), suggesting that perceived exclusion alone does not strongly predict political behaviour. Instead, demographic variables-particularly age-emerged as more meaningful predictors, with mean participation scores rising substantially from 1.65 among 14-year-olds to 5.88 among 17-year-olds, while perceived inclusion scores remained virtually unchanged across age groups. Modest gender differences were also observed, with male participants reporting slightly higher participation scores than female participants. The findings indicate that rural Ontario youth navigate their political identities in complex, individualized ways that extend beyond feelings of exclusion. The study contributes one of the first examinations of this relationship in a Canadian rural context and suggests that supporting youth political engagement requires creating age-appropriate opportunities for involvement rather than focusing solely on addressing perceptions of exclusion.

title: Grocery Retailers Substantially Reduce Food Waste through Local Demand Learning
affiliations: University of California, San Diego (UCSD),  and

detail.title: Grocery Retailers Substantially Reduce Food Waste through Local Demand Learning
detail.abstract: Grocery retailers waste billions of dollars worth of perishable food annually, yet whether they learn to reduce this waste over time, and how, remains unclear. We analyze sales, waste, and order-arrival data from 109 new-store openings of a Japanese grocery retailer, covering all perishable departments. We document substantial waste reductions after new-store openings—a pattern that holds across every store-cohort, store size, and category—and provide model-free evidence that these reductions are consistent with local, firm-side demand learning. To distinguish this mechanism from alternative explanations, we develop a Bayesian-learning extension of the Newsvendor model, derive empirical predictions, and test them against the data. We establish three findings: (1) waste rates substantially decline—56.8% after store openings—but this reduction takes about two years; (2) the waste decrease comes from stores learning not just how much inventory to stock but also which products to stock—27.4% of products are dropped within two years, indicating considerable store-level tailoring of assortments to local demand; and (3) other mechanisms—such as operational learning, demand-side learning, and changes in underlying demand, profit margins, or markdowns—cannot fully explain the waste decrease.

title: The Dual Currency Framework: A Market Mechanism for Public Goods

detail.title: The Dual Currency Framework: A Market Mechanism for Public Goods

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a second market, complementary to the Walrasian system, for the provision of public goods at unbounded scale. The mechanism generates a second currency-social currency-at the point of factor income, which agents spend in a public market where purchasing power is conditioned on alignment with the aggregate spending pattern via cosine similarity. The mechanism achieves for public goods what Walrasian equilibrium achieves for private goods: a Nash equilibrium that becomes operationally strategyindependent through price-taking at scale, with endogenous personalized prices emerging from decentralized optimization rather than central computation. It achieves sybil resistance and budget balance by construction, and local convergence to equilibrium under standard concavity conditions on agent preferences. It inverts Olson's collective action problem through a geometric mechanism that strengthens with scale. The identified limitation is that the mechanism approximates but does not achieve exact Lindahl efficiency-the irreducible cost of approximating the Olson inversion under the sybil-resistance constraint. Whether the overall Lindahl gap is small enough to constitute meaningful efficiency is an empirical question the mechanism's observable structure equips researchers to investigate.

Optimal Market State Theory: 
A Fractal Approach to Regime Classification
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
Optimal Market State Theory: 
A Fractal Approach to Regime Classification
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Optimal Market State (OMST) Theory, a new financial market framework that acts as the "Universal Translator" for market health, specifically when describing assets within the stock market. This theory defines the "Optimal Market State" (OMS) a temporary regime where an asset, sector, or industry maintains sustainable directional movement, deep liquidity, and low execution friction. Traditional models often rely on binary market classifications, failing to capture the nuanced microstructure of changing market states [1]. When describing an asset's OMS, the asset is not analyzed in a vacuum; instead, the framework relies on the asset's relationship with correlated sectors, macro indexes, and inverse assets to validate its state. Because of this, OMST acts as the ultimate "filter" for trading and investment strategies. Additionally, the Optimal Market State Efficiency percentage (OMSE%) acts as a critical decision-making tool for long-term funds, high-frequency traders, and automated systems.

title: Is Invariance Possible? The Kac Ratio as a Method for Mitigating Overfitting in Algorithmic Trading
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Is Invariance Possible? The Kac Ratio as a Method for Mitigating Overfitting in Algorithmic Trading
detail.abstract:
This article addresses one of the most critical vulnerabilities in quantitative finance and algorithmic trading: backtest overfitting and data mining bias. Traditional performance metrics, such as Sharpe ratios, frequently suffer from selection bias, identifying parameters that maximize historical returns but fail catastrophically in out-of-sample conditions. To mitigate this structural dependency, this study introduces the KaC Ratio, a novel hybrid evaluation metric that multiplies an asset’s risk-adjusted return (Sharpe Ratio) by the linearity of its cumulative equity curve (R²). To validate its empirical robustness and demonstrate its statistical invariance, a multidimensional macro-audit framework was designed. The KaC Ratio was subjected to stress tests against 20 classic and contemporary financial ratios across a cross-sectional universe of 600 systematic strategy combinations (derived from overnight and post-settlement anomalies in 60 global futures contracts). 

The experimental architecture incorporated three static validation frameworks (training/test splits of 75/25, 50/50, and 25/75) and two dynamic, iterative schemes (Walk Forward Analysis and Robust Walk Forward Analysis). Performance distributions were aggregated through a non-parametric combinatorial framework using Borda Count rankings and a custom Position-Volatility Efficiency metric (PER analysis). Empirical results demonstrate that, while traditional ratios experience severe performance degradation under information scarcity (25/75 framework), the KaC Ratio functions as an exceptional defensive shield, as it exhibits the most stable opponent ranking of all analyzed ratios, performing well under any robustness analysis employed.

title: How Italian Criminal Law Moved a European Steel Giant Before Markets Noticed

detail.title: How Italian Criminal Law Moved a European Steel Giant Before Markets Noticed
detail.abstract: This paper identifies legislative criminal immunity cycles as a mispriced equity factor in European strategic industrial assets. Using the ArcelorMittal–ILVA enforcement chain as a natural experiment, I document four enforcement events between 2019 and 2024 in which Italian criminal law produced direct, material consequences for a listed multinational, including a formal withdrawal notice and a subsequent insolvency declaration, and test whether equity markets priced these events in real time. Using daily closing prices pulled from Bloomberg Terminal, I construct a market model event study across four Tier 1 events with significance testing using the Boehmer-Musumeci-Poulsen standardized cross-sectional method. I find no statistically significant abnormal returns in short event windows around any of the three 2019 enforcement events, despite the October 2019 scudo penale removal triggering ArcelorMittal's contractual withdrawal clause within 13 days. Bloomberg terminal news records confirm zero ILVA-related coverage in the week of the legislative vote. The sole statistically significant result is a cumulative abnormal return of +15.59% in the [-1,+20] window following the withdrawal notice, reflecting market participants pricing Italian government intervention rather than the underlying criminal enforcement event. A confirmed data gap in the ArcelorMittal 5-year EUR CDS series across the entire 2019 enforcement window further suggests the credit market was structurally absent during the most consequential legal events in the company's Italian history. I argue that Italian parliamentary legislative records constitute a systematically unindexed alternative data source carrying material corporate information, and that the 13-day gap between the enforcement event and public disclosure represents a structurally exploitable information asymmetry for legislative monitors.

title: Intergenerational Redistribution in the Green Transition
affiliations: Roma Tre University - Department of Law, Banque de France and Ecole Polytechnique, Palaiseau

detail.title: Intergenerational Redistribution in the Green Transition
detail.abstract: We study the intergenerational distributional effects of carbon pricing during the green transition in an overlapping-generations New Keynesian model calibrated to euro-area household micro data. Climate policy generates systematic redistribution across cohorts through two channels: a labor-income channel, driven by wage compression and lower labor demand, and a financial-wealth channel, driven by asset revaluation and higher real returns. The laborincome channel dominates quantitatively, generating persistent welfare losses of up to 6 percent in permanent-consumption equivalents for working-age households, while retirees experience comparable gains. Revenue recycling can mitigate these asymmetries, requiring 40 to 68 percent of carbon-tax revenues to be directed toward financial-income tax relief. Monetary policy has limited influence on the overall redistributive pattern.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the conditional correlation between US equity and Treasury returns structurally shifted following the inflation episode of 2022. Using monthly data from January 2000 to March 2026, a TARCH(1,1) model characterises univariate volatility dynamics of S&P 500 log-returns, and a DCC-GARCH(1,1) model extracts a time series of conditional correlations jointly on equity and bond returns. The conditional correlation averaged 0.280 in the pre-2022 period and fell to-0.013 post-2022, a decline of 0.293 confirmed by a Chow test (F = 94.47, p < 0.001). A driver regression of the extracted correlation on TIPS breakeven inflation and the VIX finds no significant linear relationship (R 2 = 0.082), consistent with the shift operating as a discrete structural regime change rather than a continuous response to observable macroeconomic variables. Rolling outof-sample forecasts from the TARCH(1,1) produce significantly lower RMSE than a naive benchmark (0.034 versus 0.045, DM =-2.393, p = 0.021). The results indicate that the flight-to-quality mechanism broke down precisely when investors needed it most, with implications for portfolio diversification in inflationary regimes.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Neuroimaging: The Past, The Present and Its Limitations

detail.abstract: Stroke remains one of the leading causes of death and long-term disability worldwide, with rapid diagnosis being essential for effective treatment and improved patient outcomes. Neuroimaging techniques such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) play a central role in stroke diagnosis; however, manual interpretation of these scans can be time-consuming and subject to variability. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning and deep learning approaches, has emerged as a promising solution for enhancing the speed and accuracy of stroke neuroimaging analysis. This paper explores the evolution of AI in neuroimaging, from early computational models to modern convolutional neural networks and advanced architectures such as U-Net. It explores current AI applications in CT and MRI-based stroke detection, including lesion segmentation, large vessel occlusion detection, infarct core estimation, and ischemic penumbra assessment. The paper also discusses modern developments such as AI-assisted ASPECTS scoring, hybrid machine learning frameworks, and transfer learning models that have demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy and improved workflow efficiency. In addition, major limitations and concerns are addressed, including dataset bias, lack of generalizability, ethical and legal challenges, data privacy risks, clinician burnout, and others. Future directions in the field, including federated learning, explainable AI, radiomics, and precision stroke medicine are also highlighted. Overall, AI has the potential to significantly transform stroke neuroimaging by supporting faster, more reliable, and more personalized clinical decision-making, although further validation and responsible implementation remain essential for widespread clinical adoption.

title: Sticky Priors: Prediction Markets and Institutional Belief Rigidity

detail.title: Sticky Priors: Prediction Markets and Institutional Belief Rigidity
detail.abstract: This paper examines the growing role of prediction markets as decentralized mechanisms of expectation formation in environments characterized by declining institutional credibility, macroeconomic uncertainty, and informational fragmentation. We introduce the concept of Sticky Priors-the tendency of institutions, policymakers, and the public to resist Bayesian updating of their beliefs even in the face of contradicting evidence-as a unifying framework to explain why official forecasting mechanisms systematically underperform prediction markets during periods of high uncertainty. Sticky Priors are distinct from the Sticky Expectations of Mankiw and Reis (2002): where the latter describes staggered updating across heterogeneous agents, Sticky Priors describes the institutional and narrative anchoring of prior beliefs themselves, driven by political incentives, reputational concerns, and cognitive entrenchment. Drawing on rational expectations theory (Muth, 1961), Hayekian dispersed information (Hayek, 1945), the efficient market hypothesis (Fama, 1970), decision markets (Hanson, 1999), and behavioral economics (Kahneman, 2011; Thaler & Sunstein, 2008), we develop a theoretical framework that situates prediction markets as the primary mechanism capable of forcing prior updating under financial discipline. We focus primarily on Argentina-a recurring case study in institutional fragility, hyperinflation, and credibility collapse-while extending the analysis to the United States, where the Federal Reserve's 'transitory' inflation narrative of 2021 represents a paradigmatic case of institutional Sticky Priors. The evidence suggests that under conditions of high institutional stress, decentralized probabilistic markets exhibit superior responsiveness to new information precisely because they impose an immediate financial cost on agents who fail to update. We propose four testable hypotheses, including a novel hypothesis on the inverse relationship between institutional prior rigidity and prediction market accuracy, and outline an empirical agenda for future research.

title: What the Product Knows: India's Missing Intelligence Layer

detail.title: What the Product Knows: India's Missing Intelligence Layer
detail.abstract: India has invested heavily in agricultural data infrastructure — TraceNet, APEDA documentation, FSSAI licensing, digital mandis, e-NAM, Agristack. Yet product-level information remains fragmented. This synthesis paper draws on the four preceding SGPIS papers to document a structural condition: product information is generated at every stage of India's food and agriculture systems but does not accumulate into a portable, reusable product identity. The paper introduces the concept of non-accumulation in product information systems and argues that the gap is structural — not a data deficit, but an architectural absence. India has the documentation. What it lacks is a disclosure layer that makes producer-declared product information portable across buyers, institutions, and markets.

title: Autocratic Legalism and Extraterritorial Security Creep: Implications for Human Rights in Hong Kong and the 2026 Iranian Athletic Defections

detail.title: Autocratic Legalism and Extraterritorial Security Creep: Implications for Human Rights in Hong Kong and the 2026 Iranian Athletic Defections
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the systemic fragmentation of the international human rights architecture caused by contemporary national security frameworks. Utilizing a blackletter legal methodology alongside comparative case-study analysis, the study exposes an "enforcement deficit" where modern states maintain a formal veneer of international treaty compliance while effectively neutralizing civil liberties.
The paper evaluates this phenomenon through a dual-track mechanism of control. First, it analyzes the intra-territorial structural transformations within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR). It explores how localized national security legislation subverts traditional common law presumptions, establishes parallel judicial tracks, and circumvents the proportionality tests domesticated by Article 39 of the Basic Law and the Hong Kong Bill of Rights Ordinance. Second, the paper assesses the external, extraterritorial projection of state power through a dense empirical evaluation of the Islamic Republic of Iran women’s national football team during the 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup in Australia. It details how the Iranian security apparatus deployed non-lethal, digital, and proxy-based coercion against athletes' domestic families to suppress symbolic speech (Article 19 ICCPR) and force the withdrawal of valid asylum claims (Article 14 UDHR). 
Finally, the study synthesizes these internal and external legal tracks by tracing the restrictive, non-refoulement procedural pipeline of Hong Kong’s Unified Screening Mechanism (USM). It demonstrates how localized judicial activism collapses when intersecting with overriding national security mandates, leaving individuals structurally unprotected by geographic boundaries.

detail.abstract: Carbon markets have emerged as a dominant response to the perceived insufficiency of climate action. detail.abstract: The rapid buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure has transformed GPUs, TPUs, servers, networking equipment, power systems, and cooling assets from routine technology equipment into strategically significant economic assets. Under current U.S. GAAP, companies generally disclose broad property and equipment categories, depreciation methods, and estimated useful lives, but investors receive limited information about the age, utilization, workload allocation, collateral status, and obsolescence risk of AI computing hardware. This paper develops a conceptual disclosure framework for AI computing hardware and related data center infrastructure. It argues that full fair-value accounting for GPU fleets is not necessary, but that existing disclosures are increasingly insufficient for evaluating impairment indicators, depreciation estimates, collateralized financing, and expected cash flows. The paper proposes a phased disclosure approach that begins in Management's Discussion and Analysis, where management can explain the economic assumptions behind AI infrastructure investment before operational metrics are mature enough for audited PP&E footnotes. The proposed framework emphasizes disaggregation by chip generation, workload category, deployment status, useful-life assumption, utilization, natural-resource constraint, and collateral exposure. By connecting engineering and infrastructure data to financial-reporting judgments, the paper seeks to improve investor understanding of the economics and risks of the AI data center buildout.

title: Selective Index Timing via Probabilistic Gradient Boosting: Evidence from KOSPI 200

detail.title: Selective Index Timing via Probabilistic Gradient Boosting: Evidence from KOSPI 200

keywords: false signal suppression JEL Classification: G11

detail.abstract: Index-level return forecasting is a structurally low signal-to-noise problem: directional accuracy is only marginally above chance even with modern machine learning models, and false defensive signals-months in which the model triggers a position reduction but the market subsequently rises-compound into long-run underperformance. Rather than treating the point forecast as the final object, this paper explores a different question: can a probabilistic ML model's own predictive uncertainty serve as a selective decision filter, determining when its defensive signals should be acted upon and when they should be discarded? This paper introduces a proof-of-concept framework for uncertainty-based selective index timing, which we refer to as Variance-Adaptive Risk Defense (VARD). A single probabilistic gradient boosting model, trained under a Gaussian NLL objective with SGLD posterior sampling, produces-from a single inference call-a directional forecast and two complementary uncertainty estimates: aleatoric uncertainty σ 2 a (irreducible data noise) and epistemic uncertainty σ 2 e (parametric uncertainty from insufficient training signal). Rolling percentile ranks of both components serve as endogenous rejection scores: the strategy executes a defensive allocation only when both ranks fall below a pre-specified threshold, and abstains otherwise. Using KOSPI 200 monthly timing as a low-SNR empirical testbed (136-month expandingwindow OOS, 2015-2026), we show that starting from a direction-only baseline that already contains a weak timing signal, uncertainty-based rejection concentrates the model's 64 defense candidates into 19 retained actions, raising the retained-signal hit rate from 56% to 79%. The ablation decomposition provides evidence that aleatoric and epistemic components capture partially distinct false-signal regimes. The results should be interpreted as a single-market proof of concept rather than evidence of cross-market robustness: VARD refines a weak directional signal by selectively deciding when not to act on it, rather than independently creating a directional timing signal.

title: Unjust Prices
affiliations: Fordham University School of Law

detail.title: Unjust Prices

keywords: and Hyperdynamic Pricing Evokes Ancient Intuitions About

detail.abstract:
This Essay looks at the moral debate around three new pricing practices that are central to the pricing revolution: surveillance pricing, hyperdynamic pricing, and hyperexperimental pricing, I explore whether the just price tradition, which never fully left us, is present in these debates and what it might have to say about them.

All three forms of pricing, I argue, lie at the extreme on a continuum (dynamic pricing is often embraced; price gouging reviled; experiments loved; hyper-experimentation hated; personal treatment loved; surveillance pricing hated) which make them particularly interesting. Moreover, the fog of prices that results when these practices are braided together may be worthy of independent moral exploration.

I argue that moral intuitions around surveillance pricing echo both major ways of understanding just price theory: they violate the notion that the buyer is getting the common estimation of the worth, and they violate any notion of a tie to cost. The functional secrecy operates as a cousin to fraud, as it is real-time withholding of key information that a buyer would find useful. When it comes to hyperdynamic pricing, the lack of inequality between consumers softens the intuition, but the more that dynamic pricing reveals a disconnect between cost and demand, the less likely it is to be acceptable, and the more it is constant, the more it obscures the possibility of a common estimation price. When it comes to experimentation, the experiments’ intensity and ongoing nature and the intimacy of information used are all qualitative elements that can make experiment unjust because it destroys the possibility of common estimation and it means that most prices are not equal exchanges.

Finally, the braided nature of these practices leads to a fog of prices, in which the use of any technique is itself unclear, and that lack of clarity represents an independent moral harm.

title: Rawlsianism as Utilitarianism: Weak Semigroup Structures of Individual Values and Social Welfare
affiliations: Northwest University and Northwest University - School of Economics and Management

detail.title: Rawlsianism as Utilitarianism: Weak Semigroup Structures of Individual Values and Social Welfare
detail.abstract: We develop an abstract algebraic theory of weak semigroups as a basic mathematical tool for aggregating individual values into social welfare. When there exists a common individual value space that is a weak fully-rationally-ordered abelian semigroup, the space of value distributions equipped with an anonymous social welfare ordering naturally forms a social value space that is a weak rationally-ordered abelian semigroup. This social value space can never be linearly ordered, even if the common individual value space is Euclidean. Based on the weak semigroup structures of individual and social values, we can reexamine the axiomatic foundations of utilitarianism from an ordinal as well as algebraic perspective. Our analysis reveals that the axiomatization of abstract utilitarianism is quite sensitive to the underlying ordinal and algebraic structures of the common value space. In particular, under the assumptions of anonymity, the Pareto indifference principle, and the weak Pareto principle, utilitarianism over a weak strictlyrationally-ordered abelian semigroup is characterized by monotonicity, while utilitarianism over a weak strictly-rationally-ordered abelian monoid is characterized by translation invariance. Finally, we characterize Rawlsianism over any rationally ordered common value space as a special form of abstract utilitarianism.

detail.abstract: This article reflects on the Association for the Promotion of Political Economy and Law (APPEAL), formed in 2012 as the first contemporary scholarly group named for the emerging field of Law and Political Economy (LPE). APPEAL organizes academics and allies to address urgent social problems by exploring possibilities for reorienting the economy toward justice, equality, and democracy. To mobilize ideas for change, APPEAL emphasizes collaborative intellectual communities. I situate APPEAL in the context of a neoliberal political movement to capture law's power by investing in the Law and Economics message that economic power inevitably limits democracy and social justice. Though vastly outmatched in funding, APPEAL brings together experts in economics, law, and other disciplines to clarify and change influential neoliberal ideas about both law and economics. I highlight APPEAL participants' scholarship showing the interconnected social, political, and legal nature of economic power as the basis for transforming economic politics and policy.

detail.title: Explaining the Historical Rise and Recent Decline in Social Security Disability Insurance Enrollment

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Chicago, Becker Friedman Institute for Economics Working Paper No. 2026-73
publicationDetails.journalName: Becker Friedman Institute for Economics Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: After substantial growth in the 1990s and 2000s, enrollment in the U.S. Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) program has been declining since 2013. We use detailed administrative data to quantify the contributions of various factors to trends in SSDI enrollment, focusing especially on the decline in the 2010s. A statistical decomposition suggests that the vast majority of the decline in SSDI enrollment since 2013 is attributable to declines in application rates-and, to a lesser extent, award rates-within demographic groups. There is very little contribution from changes over time in demographic characteristics, eligibility, or exit from SSDI. The decline in SSDI enrollment rates is disproportionately driven by low-to-middle-skilled men who, over time, have become less likely to apply for SSDI and more likely to work. Consistent with this descriptive evidence, we present results from a causal analysis suggesting that improved labor market opportunity for less-skilled men is a key explanation for the decline in SSDI enrollment. We also investigate several other popular hypotheses for the decline in SSDI applications, including lower award rates at the appeals level, and find evidence at odds with them.
